mbm-2351.clue: The smallest umbrella is for the strawberry.
mbm-2351.quote: I read in the sun with my feet in the shade. My nephew plants a cocktail umbrella over the strawberry in my lemonade. We turn the glass together when its little patch of shade moves.

mbm-2352.clue: I made a bowl that tells on me.
mbm-2352.quote: My potter's wheel hiccupped when the cat jumped on my knee. I put a blue glaze in the wobble. Everyone at breakfast knows that bowl belongs to the cat.

mbm-2353.clue: I wanted to hear my mug cool down.
mbm-2353.quote: Fresh from the kiln, the green glaze made faint little pings. I sat with my ear near the shelf long after class. The teacher stayed too. We finished our tea without saying much.

mbm-2354.clue: The portraits in my kitchen face the toast.
mbm-2354.quote: I photographed my family through our toaster's curved side. Our cheeks got wide and Dad's glasses nearly met his ears. I taped the prints above the breakfast table.

mbm-2355.clue: I get the high note from the kettle.
mbm-2355.quote: My neighbor sings bass and I sing tenor. The old kettle whistles right between us. We wait till it boils to see if breakfast is in tune.

mbm-2356.clue: I can send a postcard without a stamp.
mbm-2356.quote: I tap my call letters to my cousin across town. One night his baby tapped a wooden spoon against the radio desk. I wrote that little rhythm into my log too.

mbm-2357.clue: One boot turns up before I do.
mbm-2357.quote: The sole print on my right hiking boot has a daisy-shaped nick. My friends follow it through the mud. When they spot a lone daisy going the wrong direction they stop for lunch.

mbm-2358.clue: I paddle till the harbor cat turns around.
mbm-2358.quote: The orange cat on the breakwater watches my kayak like a long slow fish. I pull alongside without splashing. The day she yawned instead of leaving I knew my stroke had smoothed out.

mbm-2359.clue: The ferry ticket fits my compass.
mbm-2359.quote: My ferry-boat dad taught me the wind by pointing to ripples on a map. I tuck his last ticket under my kayak compass. Our boats still go out together.

mbm-2360.clue: I sing to the short shelf first.
mbm-2360.quote: My record shelves vibrate when I find a low note. The bottom shelf holds only my mother's records. When it hums along I feel like singing another verse.

mbm-2361.quote: I pressed a thumb too hard into the arepa dough. Dad filled each dent with a little butter, and my cousins asked for mine by name. Round and perfect can wait.

mbm-2362.clue: The night sky fits in our saucepan.
mbm-2362.quote: We left a pot of rainwater outside the tent. At midnight I looked in and saw one bright constellation. My sister made me carry that pot very carefully to show her.

mbm-2363.clue: I play with a pocket full of seashells.
mbm-2363.quote: Our beach volleyball net sags lower at high tide. We move the posts up by counting six shell lengths. My job is to carry the ruler home in my shorts.

mbm-2364.quote: I cut a tiny door into our anime club's VHS storage box. Each weekly tape comes out through the door. Everybody claps, even when we're rewatching the same episode.

mbm-2365.clue: The loop has a voting booth.
mbm-2365.quote: Nobody in our mini-golf group could agree on the best hole. We dropped our pencils into cups by the exits. The little crooked loop won by one chewed pencil.

mbm-2366.clue: My pajama pocket is the remote control.
mbm-2366.quote: The batteries in Dad's TV remote kept falling out. I stitched a soft pocket around it and sewed it to my sleeve. My family asks me to point my elbow at the news.

mbm-2367.clue: I heard the zipper before I heard the wind.
mbm-2367.quote: Right after my canopy opened I could hear the little metal zipper tab tapping my collar. I thought the sky would roar. That tiny tapping was the sound I told my mother about.

mbm-2368.clue: My cinema ticket has a bite in it.
mbm-2368.quote: The usher at our old theater used a punch shaped like a crescent moon. I saved every little paper moon in a match tin. A summer of movies barely half filled it.

mbm-2369.clue: My sleeve turned into a mountain range.
mbm-2369.quote: I wore my big green sweater to model for the painters. They put a lamp by my elbow and sketched the folds. On the break we named the tallest wrinkle after the janitor.

mbm-2370.clue: One knot is for somebody else.
mbm-2370.quote: I tied my first judo belt with my teacher's hands guiding mine. My niece came to class in a too-long white belt. I knelt down and felt those same hands in mine.

mbm-2371.clue: The orange peel steers the boat.
mbm-2371.quote: Before I launch my canoe I drop a curl of orange peel in a basin of creek water to watch the eddy. When my nephew took over navigator, he brought a whole bag of oranges.

mbm-2372.clue: I save the last turn for the broom.
mbm-2372.quote: After ballroom class I sweep up. When all the chairs are stacked I take the broom through the last slow turn. Our caretaker lets the record play to the end.

mbm-2373.clue: I go upstairs just for the doorknob.
mbm-2373.quote: Our museum has a bronze newt curled around a storage-room door handle. Nobody ever opens it. I take visitors upstairs and let them find the smallest sculpture for themselves.

mbm-2374.clue: I brought one little hill back by mistake.
mbm-2374.quote: After the ridge walk I found a tiny cone inside my rolled sock. My nephew stood it upright in flour to show how our trail climbed. The kitchen got its own mountain range.

mbm-2375.clue: My best trick starts after the applause.
mbm-2375.quote: I make a little ribbon vanish behind my hand. When people bend to pick up their coats they find it tied round the hanger. It gets a second laugh without a single word.
